items.text: Eagles ruled out WR DeVonta Smith for Sunday’s game vs. Rams due to his hamstring injury.
items.implication: Hurts volume down; elevate Wicks/Goedert if healthy but Goedert also out.
items.opportunity: Dontayvion Wicks and remaining Eagles WRs see more targets/routes.

items.text: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson is out Sunday due to his sprained ankle.
items.why: Sprained ankle from Week 3; ruled out on final injury report.
items.implication: Sit Jefferson; boost to secondary Vikings pass-catchers.
items.opportunity: Increased targets/routes for Jordan Addison and others.

items.text: Jets ruled out RB Breece Hall and WR Adonai Mitchell for Sunday’s game vs. the Bears.
items.why: Injury designation leading to official out.
items.implication: Full RB workload shifts; Braelon Allen or backups elevated.
items.opportunity: Increased carries/snaps for Jets RBs behind Hall.

items.text: Kyle Shanahan said WR Mike Evans, who is dealing with a rib injury, will be a game-time decision.
items.why: Rib injury; intends to play with padding per beat.
items.opportunity: If IN, full role; if OUT, TE/WR beneficiaries.

items.text: Tough runout for Jadarian Price through first month in NFL: 1. Lost goal-line (and some base) work to Emmanuel Wilson 2. Lost pass-down work to George Holani 3. Lost fumbles in back-to-back games 4. Is hurt (chest) 5. Zach Charbonnet (ACL) back at practice. That said, Price passes eye test and has run well when given chances. Far, far, far from over for Price longer-term. Projections updated for Jadarian Price (chest).
items.why: Role erosion + chest injury + Charbonnet practicing; short-term concerns but long-term eye test positive.
items.implication: Lower short-term projections; monitor for return of role.
items.opportunity: Limited goal-line/pass-down; handcuff value if Charbonnet limited.

items.text: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is off the injury report and good to go Sunday vs. the Titans.
items.why: Off injury report after back issue; full participant.
items.implication: Start Jackson confidently; Ravens offense at full strength.

items.text: Nico Collins is good to go.
Aaron Donald is out for Sunday’s game vs. the Eagles due to his back injury. Puka Nacua is expected to play.
items.why: Hip/groin; full practice, McVay expects play, no designation.
items.implication: Start Nacua as WR1; Rams pass game boosted.

items.text: Only a 4-game sample. But with Dylan Sampson (knee) out virtually all season, Quinshon Judkins has seen a solid 13.8% target share. With Sampson healthy for most of 2025, Judkins was at 8.3%. Judkins now on pace to catch 64 passes.
items.why: Elevated target share with teammate out; pace for 64 catches.
items.implication: Higher PPR floor/ceiling for Judkins ROS while Sampson sidelined.

items.text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels officially is out Sunday.
items.implication: Backup QB start; Commanders pass game impacted.
items.opportunity: WR/TE volume may shift or decrease.

items.text: Jaylen Warren @ CLE (TNF): Warren led all running backs with a 90% snap rate last week, handling 20 of Pittsburgh's 22 RB touches. Cleveland has allowed at least 88 yards to a running back in every game this season. Full workhorse role here with Rico Dowdle out once again.
items.why: 90% snaps, 20/22 touches, Dowdle out, soft matchup.

items.text: Jeremiyah Love @ NYG: RB5 in utilization score last week, with his 26 touches outpacing his Weeks 1 and 2 combined. The Giants are allowing 5.1 YPC to opposing backs (third-most), and Love's carried a double-digit target share in every game so far.
items.why: 26 touches, high utilization, soft YPC matchup, consistent targets.

items.text: Omarion Hampton @ SEA: RB27 in utilization score this season with just a 3.5% target share and 25% route participation. His snap rate dropped to a season-low 42% in Week 3, and he played just 13% of third-down snaps. Seattle is allowing only 2.9 YPC to running backs — second-fewest in the league.
items.why: Low utilization/snaps/targets, tough run defense matchup.

items.text: Drake London @ NO: London's averaged a 35% target share and 104 yards per game in his career with Michael Penix starting, and he posted a 43.5% target share in Penix's first game back last week (9-194-0). New Orleans has allowed the fifth-most touchdowns to wide receivers this season.
items.why: Elite target share with Penix, strong prior production, soft TD matchup.
